label: last two copy steps of length-9 sequences (token-dependent, sparse)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (100% of activation mass) and almost entirely in L=9 sequences (96% of mass; L=8 has 4%, L<=6 never). It concentrates on the final copy steps: t=17 (last output, recall_idx 8) holds 58% of mass, t=16 holds 24%, and a weaker tail covers recall_idx 3-6 (t=12-15). It never fires during original input and almost never on the delimiter. Even at t=17 of L=9 it is active only about 10% of the time, so which token is fed back gates it: in_tok r, j, 2, z (and u, g, i) have elevated rates. No simple token set fixes precision, since adding a token filter raises precision to about 0.2 but cuts recall to about 0.48. The late-step L=9 predicate captures 82% of activation mass with precision of only about 0.08, so it is a position/length detector with a token-dependent gate that is not captured. Per-activation magnitude is similar at t=16 and t=17.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=15: j, r, 2, z; t=16: j, r, 2, z; t=17: r, j, 2, u) and the token being output (most: k, v, 2, i, w, o; least: 1, f, 0, q); timing cues that raise it most: L=9, t=17, recall_idx=8.
